questions: Have your eyes been moving involuntarily or “shaking” like this?
Did these eye movements begin suddenly?
Do you see double, especially when looking in a particular direction?
Has your vision become blurred, dim, or otherwise reduced?
Do you feel that the surroundings are moving or shaking when your eyes move?
Have you had dizziness or a spinning sensation?
Do you have a severe or new headache?
Do you have weakness, numbness, facial drooping, slurred speech, difficulty walking, or loss of coordination?
Have you recently had a head injury?
Do the eye movements lessen when you look at a nearby object or when you close either eye?
Have you had similar episodes before?
Do you have hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or ear pain?
Have you recently started or increased any medication, recreational drug, or alcohol use?
Do you have a history of thyroid disease, diabetes, multiple sclerosis, seizures, or other neurological illness?
orders: Urgent bedside neurologic and neuro-ophthalmic examination, including visual acuity, pupils, ocular alignment, and extraocular movements
Alternate cover test and prism measurement of ocular deviation at near and distance
Noncontrast CT of the head with CT angiography of the head and neck
MRI of the brain with diffusion-weighted imaging, susceptibility-weighted imaging, and contrast-enhanced angiography
Complete blood count, electrolytes, renal function, coagulation profile, and serum glucose
served: deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses
results: 1. Urgent bedside neurologic and neuro-ophthalmic examination, including visual acuity, pupils, ocular alignment, and extraocular movements
cranial nerve examination: bilateral ophthalmoparesis with severe limitation of extraocular movements and right exotropia; ptosis improved
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
ocular motility examination: full in all directions
pupil examination (size, light reaction): equal and reactive
visual acuity and colour vision: normal
2. Alternate cover test and prism measurement of ocular deviation at near and distance
3. Noncontrast CT of the head with CT angiography of the head and neck
CT / MR angiography (circle of Willis): no aneurysm
4. MRI of the brain with diffusion-weighted imaging, susceptibility-weighted imaging, and contrast-enhanced angiography
MRI brain with contrast: no lesion, no cranial nerve enhancement
CT / MR angiography (circle of Willis): no aneurysm
6. Complete blood count, electrolytes, renal function, coagulation profile, and serum glucose
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Functional neurological symptom disorder presenting as functional (psychogenic) ophthalmoplegia/diplopia

ALTERNATIVE 1: Ocular myasthenia gravis

ALTERNATIVE 2: Internuclear ophthalmoplegia or other brainstem demyelinating lesion

ALTERNATIVE 3: Bilateral ocular motor cranial neuropathy of another inflammatory or infectious cause
